# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS ASSOCIATED WITH TRAUMA OR NOSOCOMIAL INFECTION

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely, antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible. Two blood cultures should be drawn. Lumbar puncture (LP) should be performed in nearly all patients to obtain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for establishing diagnosis and determining infectious organism/susceptibility. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.

# Consult Neurosurgery and Infectious Diseases Removal of Infected Shunt, Drain, and Other Hardware is Required for Source

# Control Duration of Therapy

Treatment duration is typically 10-14 days depending on infection type, organism, severity, and source control. A shorter duration may be used in infections caused by P. acnes, coagulase-negative staphylococci, diptheroids, and infections with minimal CSF abnormalities.
